_comment: One-time migration payload extracted from SKILL.md as it stood on 2026-09-07. A bootstrap snapshot, not a mirror - it is correct on the day the skill shipped and goes stale from the first live reading. `aqua status` reports the age of the newest reading for exactly that reason.

display.name: Display tank
display.volume_note: Substrate depth is unrecorded, so displacement is an estimate. To settle it: during a water change, refill from a marked jug and count. Once.
display.substrate: Inert sand/gravel, planted. No buffering aquasoil.

media.housing: Fine mesh bag with a plastic closure, downstream of the mechanical pads, at least 0.5 in bypass clearance, clear of the impeller.

display.cooling: Open-top lid, 12V fans at 45 degrees across the surface, lighting raised 2-3 in, heater off or low. Evaporative cooling gives about 2.0-3.5 C below ambient, bounded by room wet-bulb.
display.water_regime: Distilled top-off only. No water changes.

ph.note: heading to 7.0-7.2 as the coral equilibrates

prior_bands._comment: Ranges observed before logging began. Context, not readings - they have no timestamps and cannot be plotted.

notes: The sensor lives in this tank, so it is the only one with continuous data.

staging.name: Staging / quarantine tank

media.housing: In the filter. Site it where there is real flow - coral in a dead corner does very little.
media.note: Undersupplied. Tiry describes it as 'only a little', and the 5 Sep hardness results are consistent with that.

staging.water_regime: Distilled top-off only. No water changes.

gh.note: also needs to converge on the display tank before any transfer

notes: No continuous sensor. Test this tank separately with the Hanna checkers, or drop the probe in and allow 2-4 minutes to settle.
Overstocked for its volume: six snails and nine shrimp in four gallons, on a filter that is weeks old, with no water changes. Four gallons gives almost no dilution buffer.
Escape-proofing and at least an inch of headspace are live requirements here, not in the display tank. Both snail species climb.
Its whole function is holding animals at display-tank parameters so a transfer causes no osmotic shock. Clean ammonia says the tank is safe; it says nothing about whether it matches.

The Kactoily probe normally lives in the display tank. It can be dropped in here to track a swap - allow 2-4 minutes to settle - but if it has been moved, say so when pasting a reading, or it will be logged against the wrong tank.
